title: Cluster synchronization
content:
## Overview

To prepare for a failover, an HA cluster keeps its configurations in sync. FortiGate HA uses a combination of both incremental and complete synchronizations. Understanding the roles of the primary and secondary members, and what gets synchronized, is key to managing a healthy HA cluster.

![Cluster synchronization](diagram:0)

## Primary FortiGate Tasks

The primary FortiGate has several synchronization and monitoring responsibilities:

- **Cluster monitoring**: broadcasts hello packets and listens for hello packets from other members; members use hello packets to identify whether other FortiGate devices are alive
- **Configuration synchronization**: synchronizes its operation-related data to secondary members, including configuration, FIB entries, DHCP leases, ARP table, FortiGuard definitions, and IPsec tunnel security associations (SAs)
- **Session synchronization** (optional): when enabled, the new primary can resume communication for sessions after a failover event, allowing existing sessions to continue with minimal or no interruption
- **Session distribution** (active-active only): distributes sessions to secondary members

Note that some configuration settings are NOT synchronized because they are device-specific: host name, HA priority, and HA override settings.

## Secondary FortiGate Tasks

Secondary members also broadcast hello packets for discovery and monitoring purposes. In **active-passive mode**, secondary devices act as standby devices: they receive synchronization data but do not process traffic. If the primary fails, the secondary devices elect a new primary.

In **active-active mode**, secondary devices process all traffic assigned to them by the primary device.

Once a cluster is in sync, configuration changes made on any member (primary or secondary) are propagated to all other members. However, it is recommended that you make configuration changes on the primary device to prevent loss of changes if there are synchronization issues.

## Synchronization Process

FortiGate HA uses both complete and incremental synchronization:

- **Complete synchronization**: when a new FortiGate joins the cluster, the primary compares its configuration checksum with the new member's checksum. If checksums don't match, the primary uploads its complete configuration to the secondary.
- **Incremental synchronization**: after the initial sync, whenever a change is made to the configuration of any cluster device, only the change is sent to all other cluster devices over the HA heartbeat link — not the full configuration.

The cluster checks every 60 seconds to ensure all devices are synchronized. If a secondary device is out of sync, its checksum is checked every 15 seconds. If the checksum doesn't match for five consecutive checks, FortiGate performs a complete resynchronization of that secondary device.

## Settings NOT Synchronized

The following configuration settings are not synchronized in HA:

- System interface settings of the HA reserved management interface and its default route
- In-band HA management interface
- HA override
- HA device priority
- Virtual cluster priority
- FortiGate host name
- HA priority setting for a ping server (dead gateway detection)
- All licenses except FortiToken licenses (serial numbers)
- Cache
- GUI dashboard widgets

> **Key terms:** HA cluster members communicate through hello packets broadcasted over the heartbeat interfaces.
